column1: # Perl fact counters: one per line, label TAB pattern (Java regex), counted over the whole file. The
# [ignore] line runs first and reads the file as perl does, leftmost region first: it blanks POD,
# comment lines, keeping the line breaks, so a sub named in the documentation or in a usage text does
# not count, and a heredoc marker inside a comment or POD inside a heredoc opens nothing. Perl 5.38's
# class and method count as packages and subs, use parent / base as modules used. "die, croak and
# confess" counts the calls that start a statement or follow or / and / || / && / //, so the German
# article in a message does not count. "environment variables read" leaves out assignments, local
# and delete. Counts are regex heuristics: a sub generated with eval or a glob assignment, an %ENV
# slice or a key in a variable is not seen, and of two heredocs started on one line (print <<A,
# <<B;) only the first body is blanked. PerlFactPatternsTest pins every case.
[ignore] POD, __END__, heredoc bodies and comment lines
